7. A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0.
B. 𝑣0 cos 𝜃.
C. 𝑣0 sin 𝜃.
D. 0.
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
Q7. A soccer ball is kicked from the ground with speed $v_0$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal (neglect air resistance). What is the ball’s speed at its highest point?
A. $v_0$
This is incorrect because the vertical component decreases to zero at the top, reducing the total speed.
B. $v_0\cos\theta$
This is correct because at maximum height the vertical velocity is zero while the horizontal component remains $v_0\cos\theta$.
C. $v_0\sin\theta$
This is incorrect because $v_0\sin\theta$ is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at the top.
D. 0
This is incorrect because the ball still has horizontal velocity at the highest point.

B. It decreases by a factor of 5.
This is incorrect because the distance change affects the force by the square, not linearly.
C. It increases by a factor of 5.
This is incorrect because scaling both charges changes the numerator by 25, not 5.
D. It increases by a factor of 25.
This is incorrect because you must also include the $r^2$ increase (also a factor of 25) which cancels.
E. It decreases by a factor of 25.
This is incorrect because increasing the charges increases the force and cancels the distance-squared decrease, rather than compounding it.

Q13. A 62 kg goalkeeper is initially at rest and catches a 145 g ball moving at 110 km/hr. Assuming the ball sticks in the glove, what is the goalkeeper’s speed immediately after the catch?

This is correct because momentum conservation for a perfectly inelastic catch gives $v = \frac{(0.145)(110\ \mathrm{km/hr} \times 1000/3600)}{62.145} \approx 0.071\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
B. 0.093 m/s
This is incorrect because it typically results from not converting km/hr to m/s correctly or using the wrong total mass.
C. 30.6 m/s
This is incorrect because it confuses the ball’s incoming speed with the combined post-catch speed.
D. 2.1 m/s
This is incorrect because it overestimates the result by neglecting the large goalkeeper mass in the denominator.
